title: Samples from the Baltic Sea anomaly test as burned organic material
summary: Dennis Asberg tells of Samples from the Baltic Sea anomaly test as burned organic material, about 2011-2012 at Baltic Sea anomaly, between Sweden and Finland, and says they saw it or took part. As told, not a fact.

tellings.quote: when we did the samples there from uh uh we take from not from the object, but from that laying on the object. Uh it was organic burned natural.

plain: Dennis Asberg, a treasure hunter, says his team took samples around 2011 and 2012 from the Baltic Sea anomaly, a strange object on the seafloor between Sweden and Finland. He tells podcast host Jesse Michels the samples came from material lying on top of the object, not from the object itself, and that they tested as organic, burned and natural, a hint that something there was once very hot.
